references.text: The prohibition against offering animals with defects is described in detail here, requiring that sacrificial animals be without blemish to be accepted by the Lord.
The burnt offering must be a male animal without defect from the herd, showing the requirement for flawless sacrifices.
Peace offerings must also be without defect, whether from the herd or the flock.
The Passover lamb was to be without defect, a one-year-old male from the sheep or goats.
Malachi rebukes the people for offering blind, lame, and sick animals, which is a direct violation of the command in Deuteronomy.
The Lord curses those who promise a flawless animal but offer one with defects, for He is a great King.
Christ is described as a lamb without defect or blemish, fulfilling the requirement for the perfect sacrifice.
Christ offered Himself without defect to God, as the ultimate flawless sacrifice.
